Plot a forest plot of test and reference comparisons

Source: R/plot_forest.R
plot_forest.Rd

Dual-mode wrapper that delegates to df_forest() for aggregation and plot_build_forest() for rendering. Accepts either:

  • raw replicate-draws data plus column-name arguments — the common one-shot mode; or

  • a precomputed forest_stats object returned by df_forest() — skip the aggregation and replot with different style / ref / ref_band / ref_band_type / ref_layout settings.

On the precomputed path, pipeline arguments (metric_name_var, metric_value_var, cov_name_var, cov_level_var, ci, sigdigits, cov_name_ref, cov_level_ref) cannot be honored because the aggregation does not run again — passing any of them aborts with a message pointing the caller at df_forest(). Only style, ref, ref_band, ref_band_type, ref_layout, show_rep, and metric are accepted on both paths.

Usage

plot_forest(
  data,
  metric = NULL,
  metric_name_var = "metric",
  metric_value_var = "value",
  cov_name_var = "cov_name",
  cov_level_var = "cov_level",
  ci = 0.9,
  sigdigits = 3,
  cov_name_ref = "Reference",
  cov_level_ref = NULL,
  ref = "reference",
  ref_band = NULL,
  ref_band_type = c("multiplicative", "additive", "absolute"),
  ref_layout = NULL,
  show_rep = FALSE,
  style = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Either raw observation/draws data (data.frame) or a forest_stats object returned by df_forest().

metric

Character scalar identifying which value of metric_name_var to render. plot_forest() renders one metric per call (no metric facet); the covariate name is the only facet dimension. If NULL (default) and stats$stats contains exactly one unique value of metric_name_var, that value is used. If NULL and multiple metrics are present, aborts and asks the caller to pick one.

metric_name_var

Column in data containing metric names. Accepts bare names or strings. Default is metric.

metric_value_var

Column in data containing replicate draws of the test/reference comparison statistic. Accepts bare names or strings. Default value.

cov_name_var

Column in data containing covariate variable names. (e.g., WTBL,FOOD, etc). Accepts bare names or strings. Default is cov_name.

cov_level_var

Column in data containing covariate levels (e.g., 70 kg). Accepts bare names or strings. Default is cov_level.

ci

Numeric scalar in (0, 1) specifying the central interval width (e.g., 0.9 for 90% CI).

sigdigits

Number of significant digits used to format the label columns. Digits are counted on the median estimate of each metric, which fixes one count of decimal places for every value of that metric ("1.00", "0.95", "2.32" for a ratio; "12500", "9500" for an exposure near 12500). Trailing zeros are kept. Default 3.

cov_name_ref

The value of cov_name_var that marks the reference rows, drawn in the reference panel at the top. Default "Reference", as in df_forest_preprocess() output; NULL for no reference row.

cov_level_ref

Optional named vector of per-covariate reference labels, e.g. c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg"). When given, the reference row is also drawn inside each named covariate panel under that label, and this becomes the default ref_layout. Unnamed covariates show no reference row. Requires cov_name_ref. Default NULL (reference panel only).

ref

The x-intercept of the vertical reference line: a numeric scalar, NULL to suppress the line, or "reference" (default) to use the estimate of the metric's reference row (the row flagged is_ref; exactly 1 for a ratio metric, the reference exposure for a raw metric). With "reference" and no reference row in the plotted metric, a warning is issued and no line is drawn.

ref_band

Length-2 increasing numeric vector (ref_band[1] < ref_band[2]) giving the equivalence band, read according to ref_band_type. Default NULL (no band).

ref_band_type

How ref_band is placed around the resolved ref: "multiplicative" (default) draws ref * ref_band, so c(0.8, 1.25) gives the bioequivalence bounds on a ratio or a raw exposure scale; "additive" draws ref + ref_band, so c(-10, 10) brackets a reference change of zero for a difference metric such as percent change from baseline; "absolute" draws ref_band as given. The first two require a resolved ref; multiplicative limits must be positive.

ref_layout

"distributed" draws the reference row inside each covariate panel named in cov_level_ref; "consolidated" draws it once in the reference panel at the top. Default NULL: distributed if df_forest() was given cov_level_ref for a covariate of metric, else consolidated.

show_rep

Logical. Display the number of replicates (the n column of the plotted rows) as a plot caption. Warns, and shows the range, when rows of the metric have different counts. Default FALSE. A caption set in the style is drawn instead, whatever this value.

style

A ggstylekit::style_spec(); default style_forest(), which documents the roles, per-covariate coloring, and theme elements. Alternatives: style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmxforest(), style_forest_pumas().

Value

a ggplot plot object

See also

Other forest plot: df_forest(), df_forest_preprocess(), is_forest_stats(), plot_build_forest(), style_forest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_pmxforest(), style_forest_pumas()

Examples

# Raw-data path: one metric per call
plot_forest(
  dplyr::filter(data_sad_pkforest, metric == "AUCRATIO"),
  cov_level_ref = attr(data_sad_pkforest, "cov_level_ref")
)


# Precomputed path: compute once, render different metrics from the same stats
stats <- df_forest(
  data_sad_pkforest,
  cov_level_ref = attr(data_sad_pkforest, "cov_level_ref")
)
plot_forest(stats, metric = "AUCRATIO")

plot_forest(stats, metric = "CMAXRATIO", ref_band = c(0.8, 1.25))


# Same stats, reference panel instead of a reference row in each covariate panel
plot_forest(stats, metric = "AUCRATIO", ref_layout = "consolidated")


# Raw exposure from the same stats: reference line at the reference
# exposure, band at 0.8 to 1.25 times it (log x-axis keeps it symmetric)
plot_forest(stats, metric = "AUC", ref_band = c(0.8, 1.25),
            style = style_forest(logx = TRUE))


# Per-covariate coloring via the style's `colors` map
plot_forest(
  stats, metric = "AUCRATIO",
  style = style_forest(colors = c(FOOD = "darkgreen", WTBL = "darkblue"))
)
